answer: A dispatch office used to print extra lock-keeper tickets and collect transit fees on every alias. A keeper may now hold only one chamber on a numbered terrace, mount a sealed quartz timing crystal with a public beat-error log, and rivet a named anchor pin into the gate before any paid transit is posted. The chamber costs 8.4 coin escrow plus four gate timings, 23 minutes apart, within 35 milliseconds of that crystal. Lock clerks match the beat-error log to the pin stamp; if two tickets share one crystal or one pin, both escrows burn and that chamber stays dark for nine epochs.
